key_insight: Pre-FEOL Al zone melting leaves junction-isolated p+ columns with no DRIE, liner, seed, Cu plating or CMP: one batch furnace step and no critical mask.
killer_doubt: Al-saturated Si (~5 mOhm-cm) makes a 10x60 um column ~40 ohm, ~1000x Cu. That fails HBM power delivery and sub-10 um pitch; TSV forming is a minor cost.
decisive_experiment: With a university lamp-gradient furnace (~$150k), drive 10 um Al dots through 60-100 um of (100) and (111) Si at 20-40 um pitch. Measure column straightness, resistance, junction leakage and capacitance after thinning.
prior_art: TGZM (Pfann 1955; Anthony and Cline, GE 1970s); Al thermomigration isolation walls in power switches (STMicro); doped-silicon vias (Silex Sil-Via) [training knowledge].

key_insight: LLM decode reads every weight once per token in a fixed order. A rotating medium sweeps everything once per revolution, which matches that access pattern with no random access.
killer_doubt: Capacity is heads x track size: 1,000 channels hold ~2.5 GB, so a 35 GB 4-bit 70B model needs ~14,000 read channels. Fixed heads cannot fly at ~nm spacing.
decisive_experiment: Paper model (~$30k): $/GB and $/(GB/s) for a fixed-head drum, counting heads, preamps and read channels at tape-class linear density. Compare with 20 Gen5 NVMe SSDs (~280 GB/s) and High Bandwidth Flash.
prior_art: IBM 650 drum and head-per-track disks, abandoned for head cost; SanDisk/SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash for weights; Apple 'LLM in a flash' [training knowledge].

key_insight: A pinned buried well keeps charge off surface states: ~1e-18 A dark current versus the ~13 fA DRAM tail. Back-injection from the floating diffusion can write it.
killer_doubt: The smallest shared-readout pixels are ~0.36 um2 versus ~0.001 um2 for 6F2 DRAM: ~300x larger, not 4-8x, so ~$100/GB (estimate). CIS hot-pixel tails persist.
decisive_experiment: Paper layout first (~$10k): the smallest pinned well, transfer gate and shared readout at a 40-65 nm CIS node. Run a CIS MPW to measure the 85 C retention tail only if it is under 0.02 um2/bit.
prior_art: 1970s CCD memory chips (Intel, Fairchild); pinned storage nodes in global-shutter pixels (Sony, Samsung, OmniVision); charge-injection pinning-voltage tests in CIS [training knowledge].

key_insight: A storage node that gates a MOS varactor changes its capacitance ~3x between depletion and inversion. The read path then draws no DC current and never connects to the node.
killer_doubt: 2T0C gain cells already read non-destructively. Resolving ~50 aF on a ~100 fF line in ns at 300 K gives ~156 e- against ~127 e- kTC noise: SNR ~1.
decisive_experiment: SPICE plus a 65 nm MPW (~$80k): a 64-cell read line with on-chip LC or ring-oscillator readout beside a current-sense 2T0C on the same die. Compare read energy, latency, area and bit error rate.
prior_art: Gate reflectometry for spin qubits (Gonzalez-Zalba et al.); IBM gated-diode 2T1D cell (Luk, Dennard); non-destructive capacitive ferroelectric reads [training knowledge].

key_insight: Reversible layers give a free second derivation of each activation, so recomputation doubles as redundancy and can catch bit errors in unprotected or low-margin activation memory.
killer_doubt: Only for training reversible architectures, and bf16 reconstruction is inexact. RevNet already gives the 2-10x memory cut; the ECC saved is ~12.5% of SRAM bits.
decisive_experiment: GPU software (~$20k): train RevViT/Reformer with faults injected into stored activations. Measure detection coverage, false-mismatch rate in bf16, and accuracy against a SECDED-protected baseline.
prior_art: RevNet (Gomez et al. 2017); Reformer (2020); exact-arithmetic reversible RNNs (MacKay et al. 2018); algorithm-based fault tolerance (Huang and Abraham 1984) [training knowledge].

key_insight: If OOM triggers freeze, checkpoint and migrate instead of a kill, undersizing is safe. Schedulers can then book the predicted median footprint and reclaim 2-3x request padding as usable DRAM.
killer_doubt: Autopilot-style rightsizing already cuts hyperscaler slack to ~23%; MemVerge resizes via checkpoints. A 64 GB pod at ~3 GB/s freezes ~20 s; CRIU breaks on GPU/TCP state.
decisive_experiment: Trace replay (~$100k): simulate median-request scheduling with checkpoint-migrate on the Google 2019 Borg and Alibaba traces. Time CRIU freeze/restore on 20 real containers and report DRAM freed per SLO miss.
prior_art: Google Autopilot (EuroSys 2020); Kubernetes VPA and in-place resize; CRIU, Kubernetes checkpoint KEP-2008; MemVerge runtime instance resizing (via search snippet).

key_insight: Bit-plane-major storage makes precision a choice at fetch time. Top bits settle many attention keys and ReLU signs, so traffic and activation energy scale with the bits actually needed.
killer_doubt: SpAtten already fetches MSBs first and LSBs only when softmax is flat, and Any-Precision LLM stores bit-planes. Tiers add nothing over bit-plane rows. A GEMV over weights cannot stop early.
decisive_experiment: Software (~$30k): from KV and weight traces of a 7-70B model at 32k context, measure bits fetched per value with MSB-first early stop. Compare with plain 4-bit KV quantization at equal accuracy.
prior_art: SpAtten progressive quantization (HPCA 2021); Any-Precision LLM bit-plane layout (ICML 2024); SnaPEA early ReLU stop (ISCA 2018); Stripes bit-serial [training knowledge].

key_insight: Data that dies before the retention limit never needs refresh. A 1 ms spec with 10x less stored charge still raises the tolerable leakage ~6x.
killer_doubt: AI DRAM capacity is weights, KV cache and optimizer state, living seconds to hours. Sub-1 ms data is likely <5% of bytes and already in SRAM.
decisive_experiment: Software (~$50k): instrument page-lifetime histograms (write to last read) on LLM training, inference serving, JVM and network workloads. Continue only if >30% of capacity lives under 10 ms.
prior_art: RANA refresh-optimized eDRAM for CNN accelerators (ISCA 2018); refresh-free eDRAM GPU register files; RAIDR and Flikker retention-aware refresh [training knowledge].

key_insight: Qualifying memory by electrical windows instead of substrate could pull depreciated, partly U.S. thin-film coating capacity into memory without building a memory fab.
killer_doubt: Coil, foil and PV lines have no sub-micron lithography. At display rules (~2 um), 1T1C gives ~5 GB/m2; at $100-300/m2 that is ~$20-60/GB versus $1.48/GB (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Paper model (~$20k): $/GB, retention and access time for IGZO 1T1C at 1.5-3 um rules on Gen-8.5 glass and on steel foil. Fund a PDK only if some tier comes in under $5/GB.
prior_art: Memory-in-pixel LCD backplanes (Sharp); flexible oxide-TFT ICs (PragmatIC, imec); open PDKs such as SkyWater 130 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Two series write devices leak only if both are outliers, so independent random-trap tails fall from p to ~p^2. In a vertical oxide 2T0C the second gate costs no footprint.
killer_doubt: Hydrogen and vacancy tails in oxide channels are spatially correlated, which breaks p^2. In Si, SN junction/GIDL leakage bypasses the stack. A planar third transistor costs ~1.3-1.5x area.
decisive_experiment: One IGZO or 28 nm MPW (~$150k) with 1 Mb arrays of 2T versus stacked-write 3T gain cells. Map retention to 1e-6 at 85 C to test whether the tail fraction scales as p^2. Pair with N-56 drift maps.
prior_art: Stack effect (Narendra et al., Intel 2001); 4T internal-feedback and built-in-redundancy gain cells (Giterman, Teman et al. 2014) (via search snippet).

key_insight: Hf/Zr-free high-k from Al, Si, O and Ti would ease both the charge wall and a materials dependence, if near-percolation enhancement could coexist with low leakage.
killer_doubt: Series model: k_eff=70 from Al2O3 (k~9) leaves ~0.8 nm of insulating gap in 6 nm. Tunneling is >1e2 A/cm2 versus ~1e-7 needed (estimate); islands trap charge.
decisive_experiment: ALD coupons (~$50k): TiN-island/Al2O3 nanolaminates from 0 to 100% of percolation. Measure C-V from 1 kHz to 1 GHz, 1 V leakage at 85 C, and hysteresis. Kill if k>30 never coexists with <1e-7 A/cm2.
prior_art: Percolative metal-polymer capacitors (giant low-frequency k); ALD Al2O3/TiO2 nanolaminate Maxwell-Wagner giant-k; metal-nanocrystal floating-gate memories [training knowledge].

key_insight: Stored exact projections r^T W cheaply measure the quantization error on the live input. That is a useful per-layer signal for when to fetch higher-precision bit-planes.
killer_doubt: A projection bounds one layer's error, not top-1 logits. Lipschitz bounds through ~80 nonlinear layers are loose by orders, so certified fallback nears 100%. Speculative decoding already gives exactness.
decisive_experiment: GPU software (~$30k): on a 7-70B model, compute per-layer projected-error estimates and propagated logit bounds and report the certified-step fraction. Compare with quantized-draft speculative decoding on HBM bytes and flash traffic.
prior_art: Freivalds checks for ML (Slalom, Tramer and Boneh 2019); quantized self-speculative decoding (QSpec 2024); Any-Precision LLM [training knowledge].
